# An exact nonaffine translation plateau and endpoint-contraction descent

This note applies the archived reflection-pair mechanism to the TRUE globally optimized center. It is a limitation on promoting the positive local centroid-defect Hessian to an unconditional strict smoothing rule. The reflection mechanism itself is not new. The quantitative conclusion is that a genuine nonaffine plateau persists arbitrarily close to the sharp mixed target, while an explicitly different endpoint contraction has strict descent until a competing source takes over.

## 1. Exact global depth from an actual reflected containment

Let d>=1, and let A,K,B be positive d-dimensional convex bodies at integer bases -1,0,1, with (A+B)/2 subset K. Let D_F(x) be ordinary raw halfspace depth in a body F and m_F its maximum, attained at some g in K for F=K. Suppose

    2g-A subset B.                                                    (1)

Then the exact maximum mixed raw depth is

    max{m_A,m_B,m_K+|A|}.                                             (2)

The point (0,g) has depth exactly m_K+|A|.

For every closed halfspace through (0,g), reflection (z,x)->(-z,2g-x) sends every missed point of {-1}x A to a captured point of {1}x B. It preserves d-dimensional measure and is injective. Thus the endpoint captured masses sum to at least |A|, including all boundary configurations. The middle contribution is at least m_K by the defining property of g. This gives the lower bound m_K+|A| at that actual point.

For every point (0,y), take any ordinary cap of K containing y. A finite integer tilt, while retaining its trace on K, captures all of A and excludes all of B. Consequently its full cap mass is its own cap mass plus |A|. Taking the infimum gives

    depth_S(0,y)<=D_K(y)+|A|<=m_K+|A|.

At either endpoint, a finite integer tilt isolates any prescribed ordinary own-fiber cap. Conversely every ambient containing halfspace captures at least that own ordinary depth. Hence the endpoint fiber maxima are exactly m_A,m_B. This proves (2) without discarding oblique caps or selecting an expected/random point. Existence of an ordinary maximizing point follows, for example, by compactness and upper semicontinuity of depth; in the simplex application below it is explicitly its centroid.

## 2. A strict nonaffine plateau arbitrarily near the sharp planar target

Put T=conv{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)}, |T|=9/2. Let a,b,c>0, and choose h with

    -h in [c-(a+b)/2]T,
    h in (b/2-a)T.                                                    (3)

The first condition presupposes c>=(a+b)/2; a zero coefficient denotes the singleton {0}. The second presupposes b>=2a. The first is exactly the compatibility of aT, h+cT, bT, and the second is exactly

    2h-aT subset bT.                                                  (4)

Indeed the three support values of -aT at the normals (-1,0),(0,-1),(1,1) are all 2a; the containment inequalities become 2h in (b-2a)T. The convex hull of these three lifted fibers is therefore an actual full-dimensional convex body with exactly these integer fibers. Its ordinary middle maximizing point is h and m_(rT)=2r^2. By (2), the exact global raw depth is

    max{2a^2, 2b^2, 2c^2+(9/2)a^2}.                                 (5)

Its mixed mass is (9/2)(a^2+b^2+c^2). If both inclusions in (3) have strict support slack, h can vary in a full open neighborhood while (5) and the total mass stay EXACTLY unchanged. These are actual globally optimized depths; neither a frozen source nor a restricted normal menu is being used.

For a concrete uniform family, set

    b=c=1, h=(1/10,0), 0<a<1/4.

The first condition in (3) has c-(a+b)/2=(1-a)/2>3/8, while -h=(-1/10,0) is strictly inside that scaled T. The second has b/2-a>1/4, and h is strictly inside that scaled T as well. The actual middle centroid is h, the endpoint-centroid midpoint is zero, so the centroid graph is nonaffine. The global maximum is the middle value in (5), since it strictly exceeds 2. Its normalized depth is exactly

    [2+(9/2)a^2]/[(9/2)(2+a^2)] > 2/9,

and tends to 2/9 as a decreases to zero. Thus strict translation-only descent is false even for an actual nonaffine family with exact global critical depth, strict compatibility, and depth arbitrarily close to the target. The small-endpoint limit is only a limit statement; every displayed a is positive and all original bodies are full dimensional.

## 3. A different actual deformation does descend

More generally, under (1), contract A about any point p in A:

    A_t=p+t(A-p), 0<t<=1.

Then A_t subset A, so midpoint compatibility with the fixed K,B and reflected containment 2g-A_t subset B both persist. The induced three-fiber hull has exactly A_t,K,B. Its endpoint ordinary maximum and area are t^d m_A and t^d |A|. Formula (2) applies at every t and gives the complete, source-switching raw optimum

    Q(t)=max{t^d m_A,m_B,m_K+t^d |A|}.                               (6)

The first entry is strictly below the third because m_A<=|A| and m_K>0. Write x=t^d |A|, k=|K|, b=|B|. The normalized depth is exactly

    max{m_B,m_K+x}/(k+b+x).                                          (7)

Where the middle source is active, (m_K+x)/(k+b+x) is strictly increasing in x, since its derivative is

    (k+b-m_K)/(k+b+x)^2>0.

Thus contracting A strictly lowers normalized depth until the possible switch m_K+x=m_B. On the endpoint-active side, m_B/(k+b+x) is strictly decreasing in x, so further contraction instead raises normalized depth. This tracks the competing source explicitly; no monotonicity across the switch is presumed.

In the concrete planar family b=c=1 above, m_K=m_B=2. For every positive x the middle source is strictly active. Contracting A toward the origin therefore strictly decreases normalized depth all the way toward its limit 2/9, while the nonzero centroid defect h remains unchanged. The limiting empty/zero-volume small fiber is not used as a positive-fiber theorem.

This example identifies an exact source-switching deformation in one rigorously controlled branch. It supplies neither a universal reflection containment nor a descent theorem for arbitrary nonaffine fibers, especially not the proper-A/zero-B critical configurations where that containment is absent.
